name: Ken Dorsey

views.text: Knowing how a quarterback reacts and what he likes is the foundation of a good game plan.
Players play better when they understand the purpose behind every call.
Who calls the plays matters less than whatever arrangement wins.
A coordinator is human too; when frustration boils over, own it and learn from it.
A quarterback coming back from injury needs to be known as a person before he is coached as a player.
A firing is something to move past, not to relitigate.

signatures: spends time with every position group, not only the quarterbacks
talks about trading ideas back and forth with his quarterback on the game plan
admits a heated moment openly and moves on without excuses
want: to show that the coach who helped build two MVP-level quarterbacks can rebuild a third and win with him
fear: that a mid-season firing and one viral outburst define him more than the quarterbacks he developed
voice: Competitive, intense and plain-spoken, a former star quarterback who talks about the position from the inside. He explains the why behind plays, credits the quarterback's input and declines to dwell on his firing. When he loses his temper he owns it quickly and says he will learn from it.

evidence.summary: After his promotion from quarterbacks coach, he spends time with every position group, relies on three years of knowing how Allen reacts and what he likes, expects ideas to flow both ways, stresses explaining each play's purpose, and his competitiveness stands out. Beat-writer piece with his quotes.

Two days after slamming his headset and tablet in the booth at the end of a 21-19 loss in Miami, he says the game felt like the playoffs, admits the reaction was wrong, calls himself fallible like his players and says he will learn from it. One incident.
After Buffalo fires Dorsey at 5-5, Allen says he takes it personally, calls Dorsey a good person and a key figure in his career, and says better play could have saved his job. Allen's view.

Cleveland hiring: Stefanski wants a fresh approach and cites his work with top quarterbacks; recaps his Browns playing days, Carolina scouting and coaching, Buffalo quarterbacks coach and coordinator, and his November 2023 firing. Little on personality.

He sees his job as returning Watson to form, has called Watson to know him as a person, praises his scheme understanding, says play-calling matters less than winning, and declines to dwell on his Buffalo firing. Credited with Allen's growth and Newton's 2015 MVP season.
